correctness.rationale: Every alternating circle has the same number of starts in each phase. For n=2r the two required counts are (ab)^r; for n=2r+1 they are a(ab)^r and b(ab)^r, giving both lower bounds directly, even with wrap or repeated windows. The overlap digraph is strongly connected: append the destination vertex after zero or one filler symbol to match the phase. When n is even the two degrees at a vertex are equal. When n is odd and a>b, the B-first vertices have incoming excess a-b, and the A-first vertices have the opposite deficit. Appending the first B letter rotates a B-first vertex bijectively onto an A-first vertex; duplicating precisely these edges a-b times balances every vertex without deleting any edge. The reverse roles and a=b follow identically or need no addition. An Euler circuit gives one circular host, not a disconnected cycle cover: successive edges share n-1 symbols, so reading their first symbols gives the edge label at each cyclic start. This also covers n=2 and singleton alphabets. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py 2` finds shortest closed covering walks by breadth-first search on vertex and covered-edge set for 11 small families. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; finite optima are corroboration, not the unbounded proof.
